clue.text: Police officer at finish of chase examining body

parts.note: an inspector is a police rank above sergeant
taken as written

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its closing letter, taken from chase

explanation.surface: A detective arrives at the end of a pursuit and inspects a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' tempts as a corpse, but 'examining body' is the definition: an official inspecting authority. 'finish of' gives E, the last letter of chase.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspectorate is a group of officials charged with checking standards, an organisation that examines.

clue.text: This month a worker's dependent on tick

indicators.note: in a down clue the worker hangs below the month abbreviation

parts.note: inst., short for ..., means of the current month in old business letters
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: This month an employee relies on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick' looks like credit, but means a moment. 'dependent on' puts ANT hanging beneath INST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is British informal for a very short moment, as in 'just a tick'.

clue.text: Breezy point up in the Levant once

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: airy means breezy, open to the wind
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A windy headland stands high in the old eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIRY + S into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the name covered the whole eastern Mediterranean coastal region, including modern Lebanon, Israel and Jordan.

clue.text: Creature ruined the marrow

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Some animal has spoilt the vegetable marrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' signals the anagram of THE MARROW. A marrow is a large British squash.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a soil-dwelling invertebrate animal, so a living thing.

clue.text: Trial sample

explanation.surface: A trial run with a specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination or experiment, and also a small portion taken for analysis or tasting.

clue.text: Oxford dreamer in debt breathed again

indicators.note: the steeple sits inside the word for debt

parts.note: in the red means in debt
Oxford is the city of dreaming spires, so one of its dreamers is a spire

explanation.surface: A dreamy Oxford student, deep in debt, finally breathes again.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold called Oxford 'that sweet city with her dreaming spires', so a dreamer there is a SPIRE. Being in the red means owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: To respire is to breathe, so respired means took breath once more.

clue.text: Sum for child, a beginner

parts.note: a tot is a small child
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A simple addition for a child, a novice at arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain, so L means beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the amount reached by adding everything up.

clue.text: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?

definitions.text: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?

parts.words: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?
parts.note: on top a word for benevolence; cryptically, a favourable testament is what the heirs named in it would feel kindly towards

explanation.surface: What benevolence do those who benefit feel?
explanation.walkthrough: Split it in two: heirs are the beneficiaries of a will, and a good one for them earns their warm feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill means friendly benevolence, while a generous will is what heirs hope for.

clue.text: Brewed pub tea a rising trend?

indicators.note: brewed means stewed or mixed, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Is pub-brewed tea a growing fashion?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' signals the anagram of PUB TEA. The question mark marks the definition as playful: upbeat suggests an upward movement or optimistic mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful and optimistic, a mood going up, and in music it is the beat on which the conductor's hand rises.

clue.text: Siege leader with forces surrounding old city attacks without warning

indicators.note: the forcing word with its leading letter goes round the ancient city
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here from Siege

parts.note: prises means forces open, as with a lever
Ur was the ancient Sumerian city of Abraham

explanation.surface: Besieging troops encircle an ancient city and storm it without notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts UR inside S + PRISES, straight after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To surprise an enemy is to catch them unawares, falling on them with no warning given.

clue.text: Soldiers not up to standard replaced on the square

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: a T-square is the draughtsman's square, so T stands for it

indicators.note: placed back, so the word for inferior is put back to front

parts.note: poor means of inferior quality

explanation.surface: Substandard troops have been swapped out on the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' reads as re-placed, put back, turning POOR into ROOP; 'on' sets that after T. 'the square' suggests a parade ground, but it is the T-square.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, such as a cavalry or artillery subdivision.

clue.text: Father in pain, but brave

indicators.note: the word for father goes inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a dull continuing pain
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad is hurting but bears it bravely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective, but here it is the noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Apache warriors were called braves, a term for a Native American fighting man.

clue.text: Remove official notice one's put up

parts.note: a D-notice is a British government notice asking editors not to publish defence secrets
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I and S
to lodge someone is to put them up for the night

explanation.surface: Take down an official notice that someone has posted.
explanation.walkthrough: A D-notice (Defence notice) is a British official request to keep a military matter out of the press, so 'official notice' gives D. 'put up' looks like posting the notice, but it means house.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to shift it from its place, knocking or forcing it out.

clue.text: The best trophy returned following advice

indicators.note: the turned trophy comes after the word for advice

parts.note: a tip is a piece of useful advice

indicators.note: returned means the word for trophy is read backwards

parts.note: a pot is slang for a sporting trophy cup

explanation.surface: The finest prize was given back after some guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns POT round, and 'following' puts it after TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop means excellent, of the highest quality, first-rate.

clue.text: Lear's man of Thermopylae did nothing in such a fashion

definitions.text: Lear's man of Thermopylae did nothing in such a fashion

parts.words: Lear's man of Thermopylae did nothing in such a fashion
parts.note: Edward Lear's limerick about an old man of Thermopylae says he never did anything correctly

explanation.surface: Edward Lear's old man of Thermopylae never managed anything in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's limerick runs 'There was an Old Man of Thermopylae, Who never did anything...'; the missing adverb is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means correctly or in the right way, the manner Lear's character never achieved.

clue.text: Eggs this saint on sometimes?

parts.note: a breakfast dish of poached eggs on muffins with hollandaise is named after a saint, so this saint's name is put on eggs, while 'eggs on' also suggests urging

explanation.surface: A saint is sometimes egged on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' reads as urging, but the clue means the dish named after the saint, eggs topped with his name on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Benedict founded Western monasticism, and his name is attached to a classic poached egg dish.

clue.text: Bloomer made by bishop in exaltation of spirit

indicators.note: the bishop letter sits inside the word for elation

parts.note: euphoria is intense elation
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A gaffe committed by a bishop in a moment of high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbias, the spurges, are flowering plants, so they bloom.

clue.text: Hold back engineers' coach

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, the British Army corps, so REs are engineers
to coach someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Stop the engineers' bus.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are abbreviated RE, and the plural REs gives RES.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to check or keep under control, preventing action.

clue.text: Weather less favourable in resort I'm touring

indicators.note: touring means moving around, so these letters travel into a new order

explanation.surface: The weather turns worse in the holiday town while I'm on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' signals the anagram of RESORT and I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormier weather is rougher and windier, hence less pleasant than before.

clue.text: Outline of singular vessel

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: The profile of a one-of-a-kind ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or summary giving the main lines only.

clue.text: Vessel holding medicine for upsets

indicators.note: the ship abbreviation contains the word for medicine

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a pill is a tablet of medicine

explanation.surface: A container holding medication is used for stomach upsets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' looks like stomach trouble, but here it is the plural noun: accidents in which things are knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill is an accidental tipping over, so spills are upsets in the sense of overturnings.

clue.text: Play school syllabus is a disgrace

explanation.surface: The curriculum at a play school is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal names its subject, so the play's school teaches this. 'Play school' suggests a nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is what Sheridan's comedy title says the school is for; the other is a public outrage or shameful affair.

clue.text: Having no canines etc, in garden thanks to these limits

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden
ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters, taken from these

explanation.surface: Something toothless in the garden is grateful for these bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' gives TE, the first and last letters of 'these'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate animals such as anteaters and sloths lack incisors and canines, the word meaning toothless.

clue.text: Dance form is a matter of taste, love

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Dancing style comes down to taste, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is nil in tennis scoring, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is an Argentine ballroom dance.

clue.text: She appeared in Venice and left with first-class return

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: return means the first-class term is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: She showed up in Venice and went off with a top-class return ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) turned round by 'return' gives IA, with the 1 standing for I. 'She appeared in Venice' means a part in a play, not a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, who pleads in court disguised as a lawyer.

clue.text: Little sign of church support for uplifting painting

indicators.note: in a down clue the church sits beneath and so supports the piece above
in a down clue uplifting means the word for painting is read bottom to top

parts.note: art covers painting
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A small sign that the church backs inspiring art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns ART to TRA, and 'support for' sets CE underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a faint mark or slight indication left behind.

clue.text: Request a piece of apple a day

indicators.note: a piece of the phrase means a run of its letters lies inside it

explanation.surface: Asking for a slice of apple each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a piece of' points to the letters running across 'apple a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal or petition.

clue.text: He may make money — about a pound?

indicators.note: the word for minting goes around the pound sign letter

parts.note: to coin is to mint money
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: A man might mint cash, around a pound or so?
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: any man with this first name. 'about' looks like 'approximately' but puts COIN round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin is a man's first name, so it stands for a male person.

clue.text: Every table includes a warning to would-be travellers

indicators.note: the two joined words take in the letter a between them

parts.note: all means every one
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Each table carries a notice for anyone hoping to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts A inside ALL + BOARD, between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The call is the guard's or conductor's cry telling passengers the vehicle is about to leave.

clue.text: Give a ring in excellent condition

explanation.surface: Ring someone to say you are in the pink.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is literally making a chime; the other is the idiom for perfectly healthy or working flawlessly.
